start_here: Say to your AI: "Read the markdown documents in a folder I granted as rows: each document's frontmatter is its fields, with the file's name, folder, size, dates, links, tags and identity, a page at a time", with {}. It runs tool:read-documents-as-list-rows and answers {"rows":[{"id":"/notes/plan.md","title":"plan","identity":"1f:a83a09f1c4b493836e2ef7ba4f403221e1e2309c337ab43769ec7ac01868c0ea","values":{"note.status":"draft","file.name":"plan.md","file.basename":"plan","file.ext":"md","file.path":"/notes/plan.md","file.folder":"/notes","file.size":53,"file.ctime":"2026-11-14T00:50:20.142Z","file.mtime":"2026-11-14T00:50:20.142Z" ...
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Read the markdown documents in a folder I granted as rows: each document's frontmatter is its fields, with the file's name, folder, size, dates, links, tags and identity, a page at a time", and give it nothing more: every input is optional.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:read-documents-as-list-rows and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Reads every .md, .markdown and .txt document under the granted folder (or `folder` inside it), skipping folders whose names start with a dot and links that point outside it, in name order, and answers one page of rows: { id (its path under the folder), title, identity (1f: and the BLAKE3 of its bytes), values } where values holds its frontmatter as note.<key> and its file facts as file.<key>.
